results.claim: The set S = {0} ∪ A ∪ [50,∞), where A = {25,26,28,30,31} ∪ [38,48] and intervals contain integers, is a numerical semigroup.
results.proof_sketch: The set contains zero and has finite complement. Every positive element is at least 25, so the sum of any two positive elements is at least 50 and belongs to S. Addition by zero preserves membership. Thus S is an additive submonoid of the nonnegative integers with finite complement.

results.claim: S has multiplicity 25, Frobenius number 49, and genus 33.
results.proof_sketch: Its smallest positive element is 25. Its complete gap set is [1,24] ∪ {27,29,32,33,34,35,36,37,49}. This set has 24 + 9 = 33 elements and maximum 49.

results.claim: The complete minimal positive generating set of S is A.
results.proof_sketch: Every element of A is less than 50, whereas any sum of two positive members of S is at least 50; hence every element of A is indecomposable. Put E = {0,1,3,5,6} and D = 25+E. Direct addition gives E+E = [0,12], so D+D contains [50,62]. Every n in [63,73] equals 25+(n−25), with n−25 in [38,48], and 74=26+48. Every n≥75 equals 25+(n−25), with n−25≥50 in S. Consequently every positive member outside A is decomposable. These decompositions also prove by induction that A generates S.

results.claim: S satisfies the source's leaf hypothesis.
results.proof_sketch: The preceding result identifies every minimal positive generator. Their maximum is 48, which is less than the Frobenius number 49. Thus every minimal positive generator is at most F, exactly as required by the given definition of a leaf.

results.claim: The nine gaps H = {27,29,32,33,34,35,36,37,49} are pseudo-Frobenius numbers.
results.proof_sketch: For x in H and every positive s in S, x+s≥27+25=52. Every integer at least 50 belongs to S. Therefore each x in H satisfies the defining universal condition.

results.claim: The seven gaps P = {13,14,15,16,17,20,22} are pseudo-Frobenius numbers.
results.proof_sketch: Write D={25,26,28,30,31}. Every positive member of S outside D is at least 38, so adding it to any x in P gives at least 51, hence an element of S. For 13≤x≤17, all elements of x+D lie in [38,48]⊆S. Moreover, 20+D={45,46,48,50,51}⊆S and 22+D={47,48,50,52,53}⊆S. These checks cover every positive s in S.

results.claim: There are no pseudo-Frobenius numbers outside H ∪ P.
results.proof_sketch: The remaining positive gaps are [1,12] ∪ {18,19,21,23,24}. For x=1,3,6, adding 26 produces a gap. For x=2,4,7,8,9,10,11,12, adding 25 produces a gap. For x=5, adding 28 produces 33. For x=18,19,21,23,24, respectively adding 31,30,28,26,25 produces 49. All these addends belong to S. Negative integers also fail: if x<−25, then x+25<0; if −25<x<0, then x+25∈[1,24]; and if x=−25, then x+26=1. Each resulting integer lies outside S. Zero and every integer above 49 already belong to S.

results.claim: The type of S is exactly 16.
results.proof_sketch: The preceding inclusion and exclusion arguments establish PF(S)=P∪H={13,14,15,16,17,20,22,27,29,32,33,34,35,36,37,49}. These are 16 distinct integers.

results.claim: S refutes the exact recorded conjecture.
results.proof_sketch: S is a leaf of genus g=33≥2. Its required division is 33=4·8+1, so q=8 and r=1. The conjecture asserts t≤2q−1=15. The verified type is t=16, violating that conclusion.

final_writeup:
The conjecture is false. An exact counterexample is

S = {0} ∪ {25,26,28,30,31} ∪ [38,48] ∪ [50,∞),

where all intervals contain integers.

Every positive element is at least 25, so the sum of two positive elements is at least 50 and belongs to S. Thus S is a numerical semigroup. Its gaps are exactly

[1,24] ∪ {27,29,32,33,34,35,36,37,49}.

Consequently its genus is 33 and its Frobenius number is 49.

To verify the leaf condition, let A={25,26,28,30,31}∪[38,48]. Every element of A is indecomposable because it is less than 50. Conversely, put E={0,1,3,5,6}. The finite identity E+E=[0,12] shows that sums of elements of 25+E cover [50,62]. Every integer in [63,73] is 25 plus an element of [38,48], and 74=26+48. For every n≥75, the decomposition n=25+(n−25) has both summands positive and in S. Therefore A is exactly the minimal positive generating set. Its maximum, 48, is below F=49, so S is a leaf.

Its pseudo-Frobenius set is exactly

{13,14,15,16,17,20,22,27,29,32,33,34,35,36,37,49}.

Indeed, each of the nine gaps at least 27 becomes an integer at least 52 after adding any positive member of S. For the seven listed smaller gaps, it suffices to inspect addition by D={25,26,28,30,31}, since every other positive member is at least 38. For 13≤x≤17, x+D⊆[38,48]; also 20+D={45,46,48,50,51} and 22+D={47,48,50,52,53}. All these sums belong to S.

Every remaining positive gap fails the required condition. For x=1,3,6, adding 26 produces a gap; for x=2,4,7,8,9,10,11,12, adding 25 produces a gap; and 5+28=33 is a gap. For x=18,19,21,23,24, respectively adding 31,30,28,26,25 produces the gap 49. Negative integers fail as well: adding 25 gives a negative integer when x<−25 and a gap in [1,24] when −25<x<0; for x=−25, adding 26 gives the gap 1. This exhausts all integers outside S and proves that its type is 16.

Finally, 33=4·8+1. The conjectured upper bound is therefore 2·8−1=15, whereas this leaf has type 16. This is a complete finite refutation of the recorded conjecture.
